Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 95, verses 1–6:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Tin (The Fig), because it opens with God's oath by the fig.

From the aims of the surah

• Affirming the honour of the human being through being created in the best form, and pointing out that he was created upon the upright nature (al-fitrah al-mustaqimah), which is Islam; and alluding to a warning of punishment for those who deny Islam, and drawing attention to the good reward of those who affirm it.

[The Tafsir]

God swears by the fig and the olive, which are well-known fruits, and He swears by Mount Sinai (Tur Sina'), upon which God spoke directly to Musa (Moses), and He swears by this secure city, which is Makkah, the place where revelation descended. Indeed, We created the human being in the best of forms, then We returned him to the Fire if he does not obey God and follow the Messengers. But those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them is a great reward that is never cut off nor diminished.

What (is it that) prompts you, O human, to deny the resurrection and the recompense, when the evidence of God Most High's power to do that is so clear?

Is not Allah, who made this Day for the separation between people, the most just of judges over all that He created? Yes indeed. So will creation be left aimlessly, neither commanded nor forbidden, neither rewarded nor punished? That is not valid, and it does not occur.
